complex-transform.t: Apply **A** to the blue square. It becomes the pink slanted shape: **stretched and sheared** in a hard-to-read way.

eigen-directions.t: A has two **eigen-directions**, **[1, 1] and [1, −1]**. They are the natural axes of this transformation.

change-basis.t: Rotate the view so the eigen-directions line up with the screen axes. This is the **P⁻¹ step**: we look at the same problem from a better angle.

diagonal-space.h: HERE A ONLY STRETCHES EACH AXIS
diagonal-space.t: In these coordinates A does something simple: it **stretches the first axis by 3 and the second by 1**. That is a **diagonal matrix D**.

scale.t: Apply D: stretch by 3 along the first axis and leave the second alone. The axes **do not affect each other**.

change-back.h: CHANGE BACK TO THE ORIGINAL COORDINATES
change-back.t: Rotate back (the **P step**). The result is exactly the slanted shape that A produced directly in the first step.

decomposition.t: **A = P D P⁻¹.** Change coordinates, scale each axis, change back: a hard transformation becomes **three simple moves**.
